source_review.notes: Checked official Cambridge publisher records and DOIs for Gusfield and Crochemore-Hancart-Lecroq, the official MIT Press fourth-edition record, the primary SIAM KMP paper, and official Unicode 17.0.0 and UAX #15 Revision 57 pages. Unicode version, annex revision, dates, and semantic limitations are explicit.

evidence: Checked alphabet, text, pattern, occurrence, slice, border, Z-value, Z-box, separator, shift, output-size, and complexity notation; checked balanced GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Inclusive Z-box intervals and half-open sequence slices are distinguished explicitly.

evidence: Recomputed naive matches (0, 5, 7) for the executable example and empty-pattern boundaries (0, 1, 2, 3).
Recomputed the 20-comparison adversarial example, selected Z-values for aabcaabxaaaz, overlapping matches for aba in ababa, and Z-values (4, 3, 2, 1) for aaaaa.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable independently asserts equality of naive and Z-based outputs.

evidence: Re-derived the inside-box initialization k=min(Z[i-l], r-i+1) from the Z-box equality.
Re-derived the equivalence s in Occ(P,T) iff Z[m+1+s] >= m for a collision-free typed separator.
Re-derived O(N) Z time by charging successful boundary-crossing comparisons to monotone advances of r and at most one stopping comparison per iteration.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The direct reduction's O(n+m) storage and O(n+m+z) time with output emission are separately stated.

evidence: Checked empty pattern, empty text, m>n, m=n, m=1, overlaps, no match, every-position matches, long borders, and separator collision.
Checked repeated-prefix worst cases, Unicode normalization length changes, malformed decoding policy, cross-chunk matches, unbounded streams, result floods, slow equality, and checkpoint boundaries.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Every boundary whose answer depends on product policy is labeled as policy rather than algorithmic necessity.

evidence: Checked the outer and inner naive-loop invariants for classification and aligned-prefix equality.
Checked exact prior Z-values, active-box equality, maximal right endpoint, capped reuse, explicit extension, and update preservation.
Checked separator freshness and absolute-coordinate requirements for resident and streaming reductions.
invariant_checking.notes: No equality beyond the active Z-box is reused without explicit comparison.

evidence: Reviewed naive soundness and completeness against exhaustive legal shifts.
Reviewed the inductive Z-value proof, including both Z[q] below and at the box-boundary cases.
Reviewed both directions of the pattern reduction and the amortized linear-time theorem under constant-time equality.
proof_review.notes: The proof hypotheses exclude undeclared equivalence, colliding separators, and nonconstant equality costs.

evidence: Audited uses of theorem, proof, exact, sound, complete, linear, lower bound, amortized, oracle, validation, and evidence.
Separated formal results from implementation tests, empirical performance, semantic policy, and named human review.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No benchmark or snippet run is presented as a universal proof.

evidence: The CPython 3.14.4 snippet exited zero with exact four-line output, matching naive and Z results and the declared empty-pattern policy.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The run records observed behavior on macOS 13.7.8 x86_64 and does not establish all-input correctness or application text semantics.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the sequence model, result contract, naive oracle, Z definition and invariant, pattern reduction, amortized proof, resident and streaming boundaries, and validation strategy. Scope remains exact single-pattern matching and leaves KMP construction to ALGE-052.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed bytes/code-points/graphemes, normalization and index projection, empty and overlap policy, separator collision, allocation, output volume, chunk boundaries, untrusted input caps, built-in search semantics, and benchmark reproducibility.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter derives prefix reuse from first principles, includes ten distinct examples spanning formal, boundary, adversarial, Unicode, streaming, and production decisions, and ends with five progressive exercises and complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external academic, Unicode-conformance, security, performance, localization, accessibility, or operational review is claimed. Results remain conditional on declared sequence, equality, normalization, separator, representation, and resource assumptions.
